newsitem.title: THAILAND: Top Thai finmin official quits after transfer.
newsitem.headline: Top Thai finmin official quits after transfer.

text.p: Thai permanent secretary for finance Chatumongol Sonakul resigned on Wednesday, one day after he was abruptly transferred by Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh to an inactive post in Government House.
Chatumongol, the top civil servant at the ministry, stepped down one day after former central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said he was forced to quit under political pressure.

Chatumongol, an outspoken career civil servant who gained respect of the business community but had rough relations with other senior ministry officials because of his abrasive style, said he had devoted more than 30 years of his life to serve the government.
The official said in a statement that he quit because Chavalit's government decided it did not require his contribution to society, a goal that he pursued since he first joined the government.
Chatumongol had in the past opposed a government plan to sell some shares of state-owned Thai Airways International Plc to a private company that operates a Bangkok tollway at a discount.
His resignation as a top official meant he also had to vacate his concurrent job as a board member of many state enterprises, including his directorship at Thai Airways.
